back: Breaks the income variance (actual − budget) down per item and product into Volume, Mix, Yield (productivity) and Price/cost sub-variances.
Intermediate budget between planned and actual: some parameters at actual values (e.g. volume), the others at budget – used to isolate each cause.
(Total actual volume × budget mix − budget volume) × budget price, per product.
(Actual volume − total actual volume × budget mix) × budget price. Favourable if the share of products with a high budget price rises.
Actual volume × (actual qty per unit − budget qty per unit) × budget cost per unit of material.
Actual volume × actual qty per unit × (actual − budget cost per unit of material). Responsibility usually lies with purchasing.
Mostly interpreted as a price/spending variance; a volume effect only if the relevant range of activity is exceeded.
Sub-variances may be linked: more volume because of lower prices; better yield thanks to more expensive material.
Slow response time, only causes measurable in income, assumes independent causes; does not always match controllability.
Faster, independent of the accounting system, flexible, facilitate learning – but variances cannot be summed; ranking is subjective.
Monitor the achievement of objectives (regulation) and confirm/adjust the performance model (learning).
